summary: This week's technology highlights focus on major artificial intelligence filings, massive hardware infrastructure investments, evolving web platform defenses against AI agents, and industrial automation.

items.title: Anthropic officially files for its public debut
items.summary: AI startup Anthropic has officially filed for an initial public offering, revealing surging revenue alongside growing enterprise adoption. The filing marks a critical milestone for AI foundation model providers scaling up commercial operations.

items.title: SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
items.summary: SpaceX secured a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing to fund AI chips and related data center infrastructure. This massive deal highlights the enormous capital necessary to build next-generation compute environments.

items.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
items.summary: Investigators detailed how cargo thieves used GPS spoofing to hijack $100 million in equipment destined for data centers. The trend reveals critical supply chain vulnerabilities targeting essential hardware infrastructure.

items.title: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
items.summary: Luxury consignment platform The RealReal updated its bot defenses after automated AI agents repeatedly held items in shopping carts to exploit reservation windows. The incident underscores new bot-mitigation challenges facing web application developers in the agentic AI era.

items.title: This startup’s self-driving excavators help dig up $600M in new funding
items.summary: Bedrock Robotics raised $600 million at a $4.1 billion valuation to accelerate development of autonomous heavy excavators. The investment addresses growing labor shortages through advanced digital engineering and robotics.
